name: Sickle Cell Vaso-occlusive Crisis

matching.reasoningTemplate: A severe, stereotyped pain episode in a patient with known sickle cell disease — often precipitated by dehydration, infection or hypoxia — indicates an acute vaso-occlusive crisis.

redFlags: Acute chest syndrome — chest pain, cough, fever, hypoxia and a new pulmonary infiltrate; can progress rapidly to ARDS and multiorgan failure
Acute splenic sequestration — rapidly falling haemoglobin with splenic enlargement
Fever in a functionally asplenic patient — high risk of overwhelming encapsulated-organism sepsis

investigations.test: FBC with reticulocyte count (baseline vs current Hb)
Assess hydration, oxygenation (SpO2/ABG) and screen for a precipitant (infection, hypoxia)
CXR if chest pain / hypoxia / fever — exclude acute chest syndrome

steps.action: Evaluate acute presentation and core clinical features of Sickle Cell Vaso-occlusive Crisis.

Targeted workup: FBC with reticulocyte count (baseline vs current Hb), Assess hydration, oxygenation (SpO2/ABG) and screen for a precipitant (infection, hypoxia), CXR if chest pain / hypoxia / fever - exclude acute chest syndrome
Apply evidence-based criteria to classify disease severity and organ dysfunction.
Initiate guideline-directed medical therapy and monitor clinical progress.
